title: 明子との帰り道  (Walking Home with Akiko)

segments.t: On a quiet residential street in Sapporo, college friends Akiko and Megumi chat warmly about Sister Tanaka as they walk toward Megumi's house. Halfway home, curious Megumi suddenly walks up to a group of schoolboys on the corner and asks to see what they are hiding, leaving Akiko flustered. Listen first for the breezy, clipped rhythm of two close friends talking.
シスター田中はホント天使。
天使だね。
そう、何でも許してくれる。
今日、恵美んち楽しみ。
ホント？
お母さんに言ってきちゃった。
何て？
今日、友達んち行くからって。
何だよ、誰？
ねえ、それ私にも見せてくれない？
おい、もう行こうぜ。
ちょっと恵美、何やってんのよ。
Casual Japanese between college friends clips endings short and melts words together. Let's hear how their lines work.
シスター田中はホント天使。
'Sister Tanaka really is an angel.' In casual talk, "honto" clips "hontou", really or truly, by shortening the final vowel. "Tenshi" means angel, combining "ten", heaven, with "shi", messenger.
天使だね。
'She really is an angel.' Repeating "tenshi" with "da ne" at the end lets Megumi echo her friend warmly, like saying 'she sure is, right?'
そう、何でも許してくれる。

'Yes, she forgives anything.' "Nan demo" pairs "nan", what, with "demo" to mean anything at all. "Yurushite kureru" joins "yurusu", forgive, with "kureru", showing the kindness comes toward the speaker.
今日、恵美んち楽しみ。

'I cannot wait to see your house today, Megumi.' Hear "Megumi-nchi"? Spoken "nchi" is a cosy contraction of "no uchi", someone's home. Ending straight on "tanoshimi", something to look forward to, sounds bright and excited.
お母さんに言ってきちゃった。

'I already told my mom before coming.' "Okaasan" means mother, and "itte kichatta" packs "itte kita", told her and came, with the casual "chatta" ending that hints 'oops, I went ahead and did it already'.
何て？
'Told her what?' Short and nimble, "nante" squeezes "nani to", saying what, into two quick beats you can use whenever you missed what someone said.
今日、友達んち行くからって。
'That I am going to visit a friend today.' Here "nchi" pops up again in "tomodachi-nchi", a friend's place. Trailing off on "tte" acts like spoken quotation marks—'saying that I am going'.
ねえ、それ私にも見せてくれない？
'Hey, could you let me see that too?' Opening with "nee" gently taps the listener on the shoulder. "Misete" means 'show me', from "miseru", to show, and "watashi ni mo" adds 'to me as well'.
おい、もう行こうぜ。
'Hey, let us get going already.' "Ikou" is the casual 'let us go' shape of "iku", to go, and rough boyish "ze" punches the suggestion with street swagger.
ちょっと恵美、何やってんのよ。

'Wait, Megumi, what are you doing?' "Chotto" here means 'hey, wait a second!' rather than 'a little'. Then "nani yatten no yo" squeezes "nani o yatte iru no yo" down to fast, exasperated friend-talk. Now let's hear their walk home again from start to finish.
シスター田中はホント天使。
天使だね。
そう、何でも許してくれる。
今日、恵美んち楽しみ。
ホント？
お母さんに言ってきちゃった。
何て？
今日、友達んち行くからって。
何だよ、誰？
ねえ、それ私にも見せてくれない？
おい、もう行こうぜ。
ちょっと恵美、何やってんのよ。
Once you spot spoken shortcuts like "nchi" for someone's house and "nante" for 'said what?', fast everyday Japanese starts unlocking right away. See you in the next scene.
またね。
